item.description: Senate Republicans voted largely along party lines Wednesday to defeat a bipartisan war powers resolution to halt military action against Iran, even though a number of GOP senators are voicing concerns about the lack of a clear game plan for ending the conflict. item.title: Judge orders Trump administration to close out goods without charging emergency tariffs
item.description: A judge overseeing the refund process for President Trump’s tariffs ordered the administration to finalize paperwork for imported goods without charging companies for the invalidated levies.

item.title: Gov. Landry appoints John Condos to LSU board
item.description: Gov. Jeff Landry named John Condos to the LSU Board of Supervisors, a day after announcing the resignation of a member representing the 3rd Congressional District.

item.title: St. Vincent de Paul closes Plank Road thrift store in Baton Rouge
item.description: A Baton Rouge thrift store run by St. Vincent de Paul of Baton Rouge has permanently closed as the nonprofit prepares to open a new outreach center next year.

item.title: AG: 11 men arrested after separate crimes against children investigations in Louisiana
item.description: Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill announced the arrest of 11 men across the state in separate crimes against children investigations.

item.title: Potato chips sold in 6 states recalled over undeclared allergen
item.description: Miss Vickie's chips were sold in six states and recalled for undeclared milk allergen.

item.title: Understanding Louisiana slang 101: A guide to local phrases
item.description: Louisiana has its own unique slang and culture, with locals using phrases like "cold drink" for soda, "making groceries" for grocery shopping, and "outchea" for "out here" to express themselves.

item.title: Port Allen residents concerned of rumors of possible ICE facility
item.description: Some Port Allen residents said they’re worried after rumors sparked in the community about the possibility of an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention or processing facility being built in the area.
